header.title: Suppl. Mag. 72: Magical handbook with love spell, spell against headache: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Supplementum Magicum
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:magic:dclp:65560:grc, from papyri.info's Digital Corpus of Literary Papyri (CC BY 3.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.
header.availability: CC BY 4.0: credit papyri.info's Digital Corpus of Literary Papyri (the source's own licence is CC BY 3.0) and this AI translation.

notes.1.1: Many letters in 1.5–7 and 1.11–16 are uncertain. ‘Loving’ in 1.13 is masculine in the Greek, though the spell speaks of a woman.

nodes.text: Extract of incantations from the [book] found
in Heliopolis in the sacred book called
[the book] of Hermes, in the inner shrine, in Egyptian
[letters]. Incantation over an apple; three times:
I will [strike] with this apple [...], I will give this drug,
timely, ever to be eaten by mortal men
and by deathless gods; she to whom I
give [it], and at whom I throw the apple, and whom I strike with the apple,
setting everything aside, may she be mad for my
love; whether she takes it in her hand or eats it
or, receiving it, sits with it in her lap, may she not
Love charm [...] of whomever you wish; say this:
for this I, NN, have taken your [eye];
